I fixed the bug, and all 6 tests pass. I ran them before the fix and the two new thousands-separator tests failed. After the fix they pass, along with the 4 existing tests.

**Cause:** `parse_price` in `inventory.py` treated every comma as a European decimal comma. `"1,234.50"` therefore became `"1.
…
 and either has a dot or has more than one comma. `"1,234.50"` gives `1234.5`, and `"$1,234,567.89"` and `"1,234,567"` also parse correctly. Everything else still goes through the old comma-to-dot path, so `"12,50"` still gives `12.5`. I didn't touch `total_value`.

A bare `"1,234"` (one comma, three digits, no dot) still parses as the decimal `1.234`, because the issue only calls a comma a thousands separator when a dot or another comma group follows.

**Tests:** I added two regression tests in `tests/test_inventory.py`, for `"1,234.50"` and for multiple groups.

I haven't committed anything.
